findings.summary: An answer cut inside its headers is read as a 200 with an empty body, so step 1 passes on it.
A chunked answer cut after its final zero-size line, or inside its trailers, is treated as whole and passes step 1.
A Content-Length written as two equal numbers is read like a non-number (no length), so a short body passes.
URLs that are ASCII but carry look-alikes of a real host (a digit for a letter, two letters for one, a percent-encoded host) are accepted by the URL rules.
A connection reset in the middle of a body fails the step with the generic no-usable-answer text, not the cut-short text; a judgement call on whether it is in scope.
No test covers a cut step 4 poll while the 5-second queue window is the limiting time, or a cut in the headers or the trailers.
In the smoke tests the section header for the URL rules now sits above the two new sections of this issue, so the older URL-rule tests are under the wrong header.
